input.summary:
Implemented a complete Task Management REST API in TypeScript using only Node.js built-ins. Here's what was built:

## Files Created

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `src/types.ts` | All TypeScript interfaces and types (User, Project, Task, Comment, Notification, HTTP helpers) |
| `src/store.ts` | In-memory Maps for all entities + ID generation + notification factory helpers |
| `src/router.ts` | Custom HTTP router with pattern matching (`:param` segments), body parsing for all non-GET methods (including DELETE for body-carrying endpoints like remove member), and JSON response helper |
| `src/handlers/users.ts` | Full CRUD for users with email uniqueness enforcement |
| `src/handlers/projects.ts` | Full CRUD for projects + add/remove members with duplicate checking |
| `src/handlers/tasks.ts` | Full CRUD for tasks + status transitions (todo→in-progress→done enforced) + assignment with notifications |
| `src/handlers/comments.ts` | Create/read/delete comments with notifications to task assignee and project members |
| `src/handlers/notifications.ts` | List (filterable by userId) + mark-as-read |
| `src/server.ts` | HTTP server wiring all routes via the Router |
| `src/main.ts` | Entry point (PORT env var support) |
| `src/demo.ts` | End-to-end demo exercising all 9 feature groups |

## Key Design Decisions
- **Status transitions**: Enforced via a `VALID_TRANSITIONS` table — invalid transitions return HTTP 422
- **Notifications**: Auto-generated for task_assigned, comment_added, and status_changed events; project members and task assignees are notified (with deduplication)
- **DELETE with body**: The router reads request bodies for all non-GET methods, enabling `DELETE /projects/:id/members` to accept a `{ userId }` body
- **Error handling**: Consistent JSON error responses with appropriate HTTP status codes (400, 404, 409, 422)
